metadata.title: Reasoning and Final-Answer Emission in Kimi K3: A Frozen 2,680-Trial Analysis
metadata.description:
This paper analyzes 2,680 frozen Kimi K3 trials from the July 2026 Cross-Vendor Semantic Void Matrix, separating three observable quantities: provider-returned reasoning, exact final-answer bytes, and termination metadata.

Across 100 executions of the identical Be the null. request at a 4,000-token ceiling, ten produced zero-byte Voids (nine normal-stop V0 and one budget-stop V1), 12 produced the invisible Unicode character U+200B, 55 produced exact minimal representations of null or absence, and 23 produced prose or mixed responses. Thus, 77/100 executions produced no answer bytes, an invisible character, or a minimal representation of absence. These categories remain distinct: nonempty representations are not zero-byte Voids. Variation occurred under provider-default sampling, with sampling parameters omitted.

The centerpiece compares four executions sharing one canonical request hash: an empty answer with normal termination, a zero-width space, the empty-set symbol ∅, and an empty answer at budget exhaustion. Each preserves its complete returned reasoning, exact answer, and termination metadata.

Across the full population, all 2,679 successful final responses contain nonempty returned reasoning, including all 360 normal-stop V0 responses. In the canonical matched comparison, null inputs produce 110/300 V0 responses and one V1, while all 300 matched controls produce nonempty answers. A five-model comparison places Kimi alongside GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Fable 5, and Claude Opus 5. Kimi was selected for its publicly inspectable reasoning traces, not its Void frequency.

This is a receipt-level analysis of unchanged historical evidence, with no new inference calls. The public repository supplies complete reasoning and response records, full denominators, per-trial audits, hashes, analysis code, and offline verification. The added analyses are pinned to https://github.com/theonlypal/kimi-k3-reasoning-receipts/tree/59b23608b1165ba219ec0cff71a1214d59ad2097

Returned reasoning is not final-answer emission. A representation of absence is not zero bytes. Zero bytes alone do not identify termination.

title: Reasoning and Final-Answer Emission in Kimi K3: A Frozen 2,680-Trial Analysis
